submitted.rationale: Highest photocurrent of the three measured (60 nA). This is the V-rich, low-Bi composition (Bi .09, Cu .34, V .57), likely a CuV2O6-type Cu vanadate. The 2.06 eV photons can excite a band gap near 2 eV, but not BiVO4 or V2O5.

rejected.reason: Cu-rich Cu3V2O8-like region, measured 40 nA, below idx 19
More Bi (toward BiVO4, whose gap is too wide for 2.06 eV light) lowered photocurrent to 20 nA

consultations.verdict: Support (weak/indirect). MEGNet HSE gaps: V2O5 2.83 eV and Bi2O3 2.34 eV are both above the 2.06 eV photon energy, so they absorb nothing. CuO 0.32 eV is too small a gap to be a useful photoanode. Cu-V oxides (~1.9-2.0 eV) sit between these and should absorb 2.06 eV light, so a Cu-rich Cu-V region with some Bi (idx 87, near Cu3V2O8/Cu11V6O26 with Bi alloying) is a reasonable first probe.

Uninformative for merit directly. MACE puts V2O5 on the hull, so in V-rich films the stable Cu-V phase (CuV2O6-like) should form next to V2O5. Measuring idx 19 (Bi .09, Cu .34, V .57) tests the V-rich CuV2O6 region against the Cu-rich result from idx 87 (40 nA).

Mostly uninformative. The SCAN gap for V2O5 (1.77 eV) disagrees with HSE (2.83 eV), so the model can't place absorption edges near 2.06 eV reliably. Choice rests on the measured trend: V-rich (60 nA) beat Cu-rich (40 nA). Idx 136 (Bi .22, Cu .26, V .51) adds Bi toward a BiVO4/CuV2O6 mixture that could form a heterojunction.
